findings.text: the inventory is re-derived by joining a rename-into-place call to a JSON serialization per enclosing definition, but that join cannot see a writer whose serialization is json.dumps and whose rename sits in a helper, so reckon/crew/follow_checkpoint.py is absent from the sixteen while carrying exactly the concept at base a928b6be: write at :187 serialises with json.dumps at :229 and calls _replace_atomically at :230, append_history at :390 rewrites the capped history the same way at :452-454, and _replace_atomically at :233 writes a pid-named sibling, fsyncs the file and the directory, then renames into place; a migration wave dispatched from this list therefore leaves that implementation behind and the section's one-implementation-per-concept target stays unreachable from it.

two further implementations are absent from the sixteen: reckon/hooks/install.py:_write_settings (:358) serialises with json.dumps through _render (:239), writes a unique sibling with write_bytes, chmods it, re-reads the original to refuse a concurrent edit and os.replace's it, and the census detector's write/write_text test cannot see write_bytes; reckon/project_state.py:_durable_replace (:163) is reached from nine call sites, at least five staging a json.dumps payload (:272-273, :1077-1084, :1744-1746, :1830-1831, :1846-1847), and it fsyncs the file, renames and then fsyncs the migration directory - a durability guarantee write_json_atomically does not carry and no inventory row records, so migrating it from this list would silently drop the directory flush.

item_verdicts.call_sites: verified 2 call sites of the new shared helper (reckon/_store.py:358, the envelope writer's renderer, and :421, write_json_atomically's); write_json_atomically itself has no production caller, which the dispatch defers to the migration nodes.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against a928b6be; c24a4e3c adds the shared helper, write_json_atomically, optional_number and the test file, 9d3cf2dd is the one-line interleave fix, and 4d3b229a and 597e785e are the fragment and the figure. All inside the declared scope, and the ruff count in reckon/_store.py is 14 at base and 14 at head with the two new files clean.
item_verdicts.done_when: the dispatch's node-level done-when is measured and logged - the four behaviours, the base and head arms with FAILED ids, the red control repeating the declared string, and the twenty-run stability log, and I reproduced 43 passed at the reviewed head 597e785e in a scratch tree at /tmp/review-head-atomic-writer - but the section's own clause, the census re-run reporting one implementation per concept, is met by no deliverable here: no census re-run is among the evidence, and the concept still carries at least nineteen implementations at the base revision, three of them absent from the inventory meant to drive the migration.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is to add the one atomic JSON writer and the one numeric decoder the duplicated copies will migrate to; reckon/_store.py:399 lands write_json_atomically beside the envelope writer, which now hands its renderer to the shared _write_through_sibling_temporary at :358 instead of repeating the atomic move, and reckon/_observations.py:21 lands optional_number, which refuses bool before the numeric check and otherwise returns float(value).
item_verdicts.manifest: read; the arms are in armed JSON form with completed:true, after_suite names revision 9d3cf2dd, a strict ancestor of the reviewed head 597e785e whose diff is docs-only (fragment and figure; git show --stat), the negative_control_log is a bare path whose first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim, and measurement_module/measurement_cwd name the scratch trees.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the four commits touch exactly the five declared paths and nothing else - reckon/_store.py, reckon/_observations.py, tests/test_one_atomic_writer_and_number_decoder.py, the evidence fragment and docs/figures/a-worker-reuses-before-it-writes/one-atomic-writer-and-one-number-decoder/writer-attributes.svg.

justifications.durability: the interleaving guard that faulted one run in twelve is repaired to compare each read-back against both complete payloads and is backed by a twenty-run log, and the no-stray-temporary guard is proven red by the declared mutation at the cited head, but no mutation falsifies the interleave guard itself, and the primitive fsyncs no directory where follow_checkpoint and project_state do.
justifications.evidence: the base and head arms, the twenty-run stability log and the red control are logged with revisions and FAILED ids, and my own re-run of the head arm at the reviewed head reproduced 43 passed, exit 0, but the fragment's central claim that the stated git-grep join yields the population below is not reproducible: applying that join per enclosing definition returns those definitions only for part of the list, and the three writers named above are invisible to it.
justifications.fit: write_json_atomically sits beside _write_json_envelope in the same idiom, the envelope writer now routes through the shared helper, optional_number matches the private-module style with its policy stated in the docstring, and no changed path, symbol or commit message carries a forbidden label or an attribution trailer.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/_store.py:399 lands write_json_atomically reusing the envelope writer's own rename step at :362 and reckon/_observations.py:21 lands optional_number, both exactly as the goal states, but the migration target set is still not the set that exists at the named revision: reckon/crew/follow_checkpoint.py:_replace_atomically, reckon/hooks/install.py:_write_settings and reckon/project_state.py:_durable_replace are absent from the sixteen, so the inventory cannot reach one implementation per concept.
justifications.scope_discipline: the four commits touch exactly the five declared paths, with no caller migration, no out-of-scope edit, no unrelated rewrite and no new ruff finding (14 in reckon/_store.py at base and at head; the two new files clean).
